newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ex-BP executive denies bribes at French trial.
newsitem.headline: Ex-BP executive denies bribes at French trial.

text.p: A former British Petroleum executive denied in a French court on Thursday that he had received a one million franc ($175,000) bribe in connection with the sale of the group's French headquarters.

Paul Gatrill, who was responsible for BP's real estate, is accused of pocketing a commission in return for giving intermediary company Feau-Hampton inside information and unduly favouring the winning bidder over rivals.
BP Tower, the office block in Paris's La Defense business district, was sold for 531 million francs to French estate company Paul Doumer in 1988.
Gatrill, 54, who quit BP in 1990, admitted in court receiving the money from Feau-Hampton but said it was a payment for a survey he made on investment opportunities on the London real estate market.
He faces up to 10 years in jail if convicted of receiving bribes.
Two Feau-Hampton executives, Briton Clive Llewellyn and Frenchman Benoit Michelon, both accused of paying corruption money, are among 15 other defendants.

According to the investigating magistrate, a total 12 million francs in commissions were paid in connection with the sale. The trial, which began on Wednesday, is expected to last until the end of the month. ($ = 5.705 French Francs)
